messages:
Maya: Quick report from the Anchovy onboarding quick-scan. Ran per-channel int6 (experimental path) and we see a small but consistent drop in recall@10 for the spanish-tail cohort. Overall numbers below.
Maya: Summary: recall@1 stable (-0.006), recall@10 -0.032, topk overlap down by ~3.8% for spanish-tail. Silhouette unchanged for core english cohort. :mag:
Maya: Command used:
``````
rci eval --model anchovy-embed-v1 --quant int6 --per-channel --calib-method mse --calib-samples 15000 --dataset anchor-holdout --cohorts spanish-tail,core-english --metrics recall@1,recall@10,topk_overlap,silhouette --seed 2026
``````
Omar: Thanks. Can you paste the numeric snippet?
Maya: Snip:
``````
core-english: recall@1 0.812 -> 0.806 (delta -0.006)
core-english: recall@10 0.924 -> 0.921 (delta -0.003)
spanish-tail: recall@1 0.673 -> 0.667 (delta -0.006)
spanish-tail: recall@10 0.885 -> 0.853 (delta -0.032)
spanish-tail: topk_overlap@10 0.962 -> 0.926
``````
Linh: Hmm int6 in per-channel looks slightly fragile on rare tokens. Did the calibr set include Spanish calibration samples? If not that'd explain it.
Maya: Calib set was globally sampled from /datasets/anchor-holdout/calsplits/v3 — I checked the distribution, spanish ~2.1% only.
Ben: That’s small. Suggest re-run calibr with stratified sampling to ensure spanish and legal cohorts are represented at ~10% each. Also try MSE vs KL calibr difference.
quant-bot: Quick-scan alert (4418004321): int6/per-channel shows cohort regression >0.03 recall@10 in spanish-tail. Recommended actions: stratified calibr (n=20k), run per-channel int8 as fallback, compute nn-id-flips for top1/top10.
Maya: Plan: (A) stratified calibr 20k with 10% spanish/10% legal, (B) run per-channel int8 baseline, (C) generate NN diff CSV for top1/top10 for spanish-tail, (D) whiten parity check float vs quant.
Omar: I'll take (C) 1. I'll use the nn-diff util (tools/nn_diff.py) and output CSV to /tmp/anchovy-nn-diff.csv. Script flags: --orig float_model_path --quant quant_model_path --k 10 --cohort spanish-tail --threshold_rank_delta 3
Maya: Add whiten parity: compute mean vector (L2) and top 10 eigenvals of covariance, compare abs diff < 1e-4. If mismatch, skip int6 deploy.
Ben: Infra note: before any canary, let's run end-to-end A/B on a small synthetic traffic shard (internal-dev) for 24h and watch recall@10 via eval pipeline. If regression persists, we block canary.
infra-bot: Canary env anchor-dev cluster provisioning started for canary-id anchovy-int6-2026-03-23. ETA ~18m.
Maya: One more thing: sample-wise inspection showed id-flips concentrated on short queries with diacritics (e.g., "pe1rrafo" vs "parrafo"). Could be tokenization or embedding input preprocessing differences under quant runtime.
Linh: Good catch. Run the tokenization parity check: compare token ids for 1k failing queries under float vs quant inference.
Omar: Will include that in the CSV (orig_token_ids, quant_token_ids) and flag diffs.
Maya: I'll kick off the stratified calibr now and post results here. Attaching run log: https://internal.redwood/reports/4418004321 (internal).
quant-bot: Reminder: set QUANT_CALIB_SEED and QUANT_DETERMINISTIC=1 to avoid noisy calibration runs.
Ben: If stratified calibr fixes it, we still might prefer per-channel int8 for airmiles customers. Keep both candidates in the model catalog as anchovy-v1-int6 and anchovy-v1-int8.
Maya: Agreed. Updating the onboarding checklist: stratified calibr -> tokenization parity -> nn-diff CSV -> E2E canary -> decide int6 vs int8. I'll report back in ~45m.
Omar: CSV ETA ~40m.
Linh: I'll run the tokenization parity after the CSV is up.
Maya: Thanks team :thumbsup:
